messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "*"Things feel like they’re holding for now—no big cracks, but the walls are leaning. The old guard is still in charge, but the younger ones are getting twitchy, and the patrols aren’t where they used to be. Keep your ears open, but don’t change your steps yet—just watch which way the wind’s blowing."*"
Sender 2: "*"Things feel like they’re holding—but just barely. The regime’s still in control, but the cracks are showing in weird ways: security’s out but not pushing, the money’s shaky but not broken, and even the bureaucrats are dragging their feet like they’re waiting for something. People are talking more, but no one’s sure if it’s real or just nerves. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet—this could go either way fast."*"
Sender 3: "*"The air feels lighter, but not careless—like the pause before a storm either breaks or passes. The inner circle’s quiet, the streets are humming with whispers, and the money’s still moving, but no one’s packing their bags just yet. Keep your eyes open, your plans loose, and your ears to the ground—this could go either way, and fast."*"
Sender 4: "*"The walls are cracking, but no one’s sure if it’s the foundation or just the paint. The generals are taking their vacations on time, the pharmacist is stocking up like it’s 1998, and the courts are suddenly doing their job—so either the regime’s getting sloppy, or they’re saving their bullets for something worse. Either way, the air smells like rain, but no one knows if it’s a storm or just humidity. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet."*"
Sender 5: "*"Things feel like they’re holding, but just barely—like a dam with too much pressure behind it. The cracks aren’t showing yet, but the water’s rising, and no one’s sure which way it’ll break. Stay sharp, but don’t let it show."*"
Sender 6: "*"The top dogs are all still sitting at the same table, and the soldiers aren’t packing their bags—yet. The streets are quiet, but not in a way that feels like the calm before the storm, more like everyone’s just too tired to look up. Still, the warehouses near the border are fuller than usual, and the regime’s voice is drowning out everything else. For now, the machine keeps humming, but we all know how machines can stall when the pressure builds."*"
Sender 7: "*"Things feel quieter than they did last week, but it’s the quiet of a room where everyone’s holding their breath—not the quiet of peace. Some are packing bags, others are acting like nothing’s wrong, and the regime’s still spending more to keep the lid on than it wants to admit. Let’s stay sharp, but no sudden moves—we don’t know which way the wind will turn if the wrong person stumbles."*"
Sender 8: "*"The air feels different—like the quiet before something shifts, not the calm of control. The jokes are sharper, the cracks in the facade are showing, and even the bureaucrats seem to be holding their breath. Stay sharp, but don’t let them see you flinch."*"
Sender 9: "*"Looks like the regime’s dug in deeper than ever—cabinet’s running smoother than ever, payments on time, even the football crowds are back. No cracks, just the same old noise from the top. Still, keep your eyes open—quiet doesn’t always mean safe."*"
Sender 10: "*"The air feels different—like everyone’s holding their breath but also leaning in, waiting for the right moment to exhale. The regime’s still standing, but it’s like watching a house of cards: one wrong move, and the whole thing could tilt. Stay sharp, stay quiet, but don’t assume the game’s over—just that the rules might be changing soon."*"
Sender 11: "*"The walls are holding—for now. The usual faces are still in their seats, the markets are moving like nothing’s wrong, and the neighbors are keeping their heads down, but the pharmacist’s stockpile says they’re not as calm as they pretend. We’re not out of the woods, but the fire’s not spreading yet."*"
Sender 12: "*"The air feels different—less like a storm coming, more like the ground shifting under our feet. The top is still holding, but the cracks are there if you know where to look. Let’s keep our eyes open and our steps quiet—this isn’t the time to assume anything."*"
Sender 13: "*"The air feels different—less panic, more quiet planning. The usual alarms are muted, but the sermons are getting sharper, and the checkpoints are thinning. Either they’re overconfident, or they’re saving their strength for something else. Stay sharp, but don’t let the calm fool you."*"
Sender 14: "*"Looks like the walls are holding—stronger than we feared, even. The old guard is locked in, the money’s flowing, and the streets are quiet. But don’t let the sloppy censorship fool you—if they’re getting lazy, it’s because they’re sure they’ve already won."*"
Sender 15: "*"The air feels different—less like a storm coming, more like the ground shifting under our feet. The regime’s still standing, but it’s holding on by habit more than strength, and the cracks are there if you know where to look. Let’s keep our eyes open and our plans quiet—this isn’t the time to move, but it might be the time to get ready."*"
Sender 16: "*"The air feels different—like a storm that might pass or break open, but no one’s sure which. The regime’s still building for the long haul, but the cracks are there if you know where to look. Stay sharp, but don’t assume anything yet."*"
Sender 17: "*"The walls are cracking, but the foundation’s still solid—just listen to how the echoes bounce. The song’s playing louder, but the lights stay on, and the doormen haven’t even flinched. Yet."*"
Sender 18: "*"Looks like the usual—no cracks in the walls, just the same old paint chipping. The boss’s old rival is suddenly singing his praises, the stadiums are packed, and the hospitals aren’t overflowing with nervous breakdowns. They’re still in control, but if anyone’s counting on them stumbling, they might be waiting a while. Stay sharp, but no need to panic—yet."*"
Sender 19: "*"The walls are still standing, but the paint’s starting to crack—just in places you wouldn’t notice unless you’re looking. The usual players are still at the table, but someone’s shuffling the deck quietly, and the new hands don’t know the rules yet. Keep your head down, but maybe… just maybe, the wind’s shifting. Let’s talk soon—over tea, like always."*"
Sender 20: "*"The air feels different—like the moment before a storm when the wind drops, but the clouds are already too heavy to hold. The usual whispers are louder now, but the silence from the top is what worries me. Stay sharp, but don’t rush—this isn’t over yet."*"
Sender 21: "*"The walls are still standing, but the paint’s starting to crack in places—just not where you’d expect. The usual suspects are still at the table, but the new faces make me wonder if they’re preparing for a long winter or just pretending it’s summer. Either way, the heat’s still on, and no one’s turning down the stove yet."*"
Sender 22: "*"The air feels heavier than usual—like everyone’s holding their breath, but the walls are still standing. The usual cracks aren’t showing, and the guards are marching in step, but something’s shifting under the surface. Let’s keep our eyes open and our voices quiet for now."*"
Sender 23: "*"The air feels charged but no one’s sure which way it’ll break—some say the cracks are showing, others say the walls are holding. The patrols are shifting, the money’s moving funny, and even the insiders are hedging their bets. Could go either way, but if something sparks it, we’ll know soon enough."*"
Sender 24: "*"Things are holding, but barely—like a stack of plates someone’s trying to balance with one hand. The regime’s still in charge, but the cracks are there if you know where to look. Let’s stay sharp, but no sudden moves—we don’t know how long this fragile quiet lasts."*"
Sender 25: "*"Things feel like they’re holding, but just barely—like a dam with too many cracks. The air’s different now: even the cautious ones are testing the water, and the young are getting restless, but the old hands are still whispering, ‘Wait.’ The regime’s grip looks tight, but the way the military’s moving and the money’s shifting… it’s all a little too careful. Something’s off. Stay sharp, but don’t rush—this isn’t the time to bet on anything."*"

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 25 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 25.
